recent_posts.title: Rails Containerization Best Practices
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to containerizing Rails 8.1 applications using Docker and Kamal 2. Covers multistage builds to reduce image size by 50-70%, running containers as nonroot users, scanning for CVEs with Docker Scout in CI, configuring Puma for containerized environments, zero-downtime deployments with health checks, database migration hooks, horizontal/vertical scaling strategies, and a pre-merge checklist to enforce security and correctness standards.

recent_posts.title: My Ever-Improving AI Setup for Rails Work With gbrain and gstack
recent_posts.summary: A detailed personal workflow for integrating multiple AI tools into Rails development while maintaining strict engineering gates. The setup uses Perplexity for research, Claude Code for long-context repo work, Codex for focused execution, gbrain for private persistent memory, gstack for repeatable workflows, CodeRabbit for PR review, Copilot for inline and delegated tasks, and Superconductor for parallel agents with isolated worktrees. Hard rules include never merging AI-generated code without CI green and reviewer sign-off, keeping private data out of prompts, and treating model changes as deploys. A case study covers the Uploadcare Ruby and Rails gem v5 rewrite, showing how AI accelerated review and documentation while human gates and tests remained mandatory. The post emphasizes measuring useful metrics like merge time and eval failures rather than percentage of code written by AI.

recent_posts.title: Rails Security Best Practices: A Comprehensive Guide
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive overview of Rails security features from version 1 through 8.1.3, covering built-in protections (CSRF, XSS, SQL injection, strong parameters, encrypted credentials, rate limiting) and what remains the developer's responsibility (authorization, 2FA, audit logging, OAuth, account lockout). Includes a production security checklist, a timeline of security features per Rails version, and recommended gems for gaps not covered by Rails core like Pundit, Devise, and rack-attack. Emphasizes that missing authorization on tenant-scoped data is the most common serious Rails security bug.

recent_posts.title: Rails Authorization Patterns: Pundit, CanCanCan, and Action Policy
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to Rails authorization covering three main approaches: Pundit, CanCanCan, and Action Policy. Explains when to use each library, the critical 'scope before find' pattern to prevent IDOR and cross-tenant data leaks, how to write tests that catch access-control bugs, and provides a pre-merge authorization checklist. Pundit is recommended as the default for serious Rails products due to its explicitness and testability.

recent_posts.title: Building a Private Karpathy-Style LLM Wiki With gbrain and gstack
recent_posts.summary: A developer describes building a private AI assistant memory system using three components: a Karpathy-style LLM Wiki for durable structured knowledge, gbrain for distilling personal work signals from GitHub PRs, emails, Slack, and other sources, and gstack for applying that memory in daily Rails coding workflows. The architecture keeps raw private data local-only, uses redaction before any public export, and enforces mandatory human review gates before merging. The result is an AI coding assistant that starts from the developer's own review preferences, Rails patterns, and shipping standards rather than generic defaults. The post also serves as a services pitch for CTO AI transformation work.

recent_posts.title: Different Approaches to Debugging Query Performance in Rails
recent_posts.summary: A systematic guide to debugging slow database queries in Rails applications. Covers built-in Rails tools including the `explain` method (with Rails 7.1 enhancements), `load_async`, ActiveSupport::Notifications, query log tags, and strict loading mode. Also covers essential gems like Bullet, rack-mini-profiler, and prosopite. Includes database-specific tools for PostgreSQL (pg_stat_statements, PgHero, pgBadger), MySQL (Performance Schema, pt-query-digest), and SQLite (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN). Addresses Rails 8 specifics including SQLite as a production database and Solid Cache's impact on query logs. Concludes with a five-step practical debugging workflow and production monitoring options.

recent_posts.title: Ruby Concurrency Beyond Fibers: Threads, Ractors, and True Parallelism
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to Ruby's concurrency primitives beyond Fibers, covering Threads, Ractors, and the Async gem. Explains the Global Virtual Machine Lock (GVL) and its impact on parallelism, when each primitive is appropriate, and how to combine them for mixed workloads. Includes a comparison table of Fibers, Threads, and Ractors by memory usage, parallelism, and use case, plus a decision guide for choosing the right approach.

recent_posts.title: Upgrading from Rails 7.2 to Rails 8 - The Latest and Greatest
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to upgrading a Rails application from 7.2 to Rails 8, covering Ruby 3.4 upgrade with YJIT, Solid Queue as a Redis-free background job queue, Solid Cache and Solid Cable for database-backed caching and WebSockets, the new built-in authentication generator as a Devise alternative, PWA support, breaking changes (minimal), and deployment with Kamal 2. Includes decision guidance on when to keep existing infrastructure (Sidekiq, Redis, Devise) versus adopting the new Solid gems, plus conservative/progressive/aggressive migration strategies.

recent_posts.title: Upgrading from Rails 6.1 to Rails 7 - The Modern Stack
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to upgrading a Rails 6.1 application to Rails 7, covering Ruby 3 migration (including YJIT enablement and keyword argument fixes), Gemfile updates, JavaScript strategy selection (Import Maps vs Webpacker/jsbundling), Hotwire installation (Turbo Drive, Frames, Streams, and Stimulus), ActiveRecord encryption for sensitive attributes, new query methods like `sole` and `load_async`, breaking changes (ActiveStorage::Current removal, Zeitwerk-only autoloading, button_to HTML change), testing updates for Turbo, and deployment considerations. Includes a practical upgrade checklist and common gotchas.

recent_posts.title: Why Ruby on Rails remains ideal for MVP development in 2026
recent_posts.summary: Ruby on Rails continues to excel as an MVP framework in 2026 due to its convention-over-configuration philosophy, rapid scaffolding capabilities, and batteries-included approach. Rails 8 now provides built-in authentication, background jobs (Solid Queue), caching (Solid Cache), and WebSocket support (Solid Cable) without external dependencies. The framework's Active Record ORM simplifies database interactions, while modern frontend integration through Hotwire or React/Vue enables reactive experiences. Deployment is straightforward with platforms like Heroku, Render, and Fly.io, or using Kamal for custom servers. Success stories include Airbnb, Shopify, and Basecamp, all of which started as Rails MVPs. The framework balances speed to market with scalability, making it ideal for startups validating business ideas quickly.
